guitar.evidence: Jimi Hendrix's white Fender Stratocaster (played upside-down/restrung for a right-handed guitar as a left-handed player) is one of the most iconic guitar associations in rock history.

tone.target: nasal fuzz-wah Hendrix lead with upper-mid bite
tone.profile: nasal fuzz-wah Hendrix lead with upper-mid bite
tone.summary: A high-gain signal chain utilizing Fuzz/Red Haze for the core tone, followed by a Wah pedal sweep, feeding into a UK 45 or UK SLP style amplifier simulation with a vintage cabinet.

rig.name: Jimi Hendrix - Purple Haze - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and unwanted noise from high-gain fuzz circuits.
Simulate the Fuzz Face style fuzz required for Hendrix's signature sound.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is a good substitute for classic fuzz, though dedicated Fuzz models would be ideal.

blocks.purpose: Provide the central and sweeping wah effect crucial to 'Purple Haze'.
Provide slight boost and upper-mid bite for lead lines without muddying the fuzz.
blocks.gap: Using Boost here acts as a mild EQ/overdrive lift, compensating for potential loss of clarity after heavy fuzz.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall/Super Lead tone and provide necessary amp breakup for classic rock feel.
Provide the classic British 4x12 cabinet sound associated with Marshall gear.
Enhance the upper-mids and bite in the lead tone, compensating for fuzz saturation.
Optional subtle modulation for added depth (kept off to avoid conflicting with the raw fuzz tone).
blocks.gap: The prompt explicitly avoids chorus, so this module is included but deactivated. A better choice would be a simple Tremolo or Room reverb.

blocks.purpose: Add a subtle sense of space and sustain without sounding overly wet or distracting.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and upper-mid bite.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic British amp sound.
